report.tagline: An Asia-focused travel booking app, owned by Booking Holdings, known for cheap hotel deals across Asia.
report.simpleSummary: Agoda is a travel app where you book hotels, homes, flights and activities, mostly for trips in Asia. It is popular with Indians travelling to Thailand, Bali, Vietnam or Dubai because it often shows the lowest hotel prices. It began in Bangkok and is now part of Booking Holdings, the same group as Booking.com. Agoda keeps a cut, or a markup, on each booking.

overview.whatItDoes: Agoda is an online travel agency (OTA) that sells hotel rooms, holiday homes, flights, activities and airport transfers. It is strongest in Southeast Asia, India, Japan and Korea. Guests usually pay Agoda upfront, and Agoda pays the hotel after the stay.
howItWorks: Hotels and hosts list rooms on Agoda's YCS partner system, and Agoda also pulls rooms from Booking.com and wholesalers.
Guests search and compare prices, often seeing big strike-through discounts and member-only deals.
Most bookings are prepaid to Agoda, so Agoda handles payment in many currencies.
Agoda keeps a commission or a markup between what it pays the hotel and what the guest pays.
AgodaCash rewards, VIP tiers and app-only deals bring guests back.
overview.valueProposition: The cheapest-looking deals for stays across Asia, in local languages and currencies, including small hotels and homes that global sites miss.

businessModel.summary: Agoda mostly uses a merchant model: guests pay Agoda upfront, and Agoda pays the hotel later at a lower price. The gap, usually about 15% to 20%, is Agoda's revenue. It also earns from flights, activities and ads.

revenueStreams.detail: Commission or markup on prepaid stays. The main source.
Fees and margins on flight tickets.
Commissions on tours and airport rides.
Hotels pay for better placement and deals.
Currency conversion margins on prepaid bookings.

businessModel.pricing: Free for travellers; prices include deals and show taxes at checkout. Hotels pay commission of roughly 15% to 20%, not public.
costDrivers: Google and metasearch ads such as Trivago and Skyscanner
Large tech team in Bangkok and other hubs
businessModel.unitEconomics: Rough example. An Indian guest books 3 nights in Bangkok at ₹4,000 a night, so ₹12,000. Agoda might keep about ₹2,000 (around 17%). If the guest came from a Google ad or price comparison site, Agoda might spend ₹600 to ₹900 for that click. AgodaCash and discounts may take another ₹300. Payment and support costs add ₹200. So Agoda keeps around ₹600 to ₹900 on a first booking, and more on a repeat booking through the app.

howTheyGetUsers: Google hotel ads and metasearch sites, where Agoda bids for the cheapest price slot
Partnerships with banks, airlines and wallets in Asia
whatBringsUsersBack: Habit of checking Agoda first for Asian trips
growth.moat: Agoda has deep supply of small Asian hotels and homes, local payment options, and Booking Holdings' scale behind it. Its large engineering team runs many price and design tests. Rivals can copy discounts, but building supply in thousands of Asian towns takes years.

competitors.name: Booking.com
competitors.positioning: Same parent; global hotel leader, strongest in Europe.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Agoda is cheaper and stronger in Asia, mostly prepaid; Booking.com leads in Europe with pay-at-hotel options.

competitors.name: MakeMyTrip
competitors.positioning: India's biggest OTA with flights, buses and packages.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Agoda is often cheaper for Southeast Asia hotels; MakeMyTrip wins on Indian domestic trips and brand trust.

competitors.name: Trip.com
competitors.positioning: Chinese OTA growing fast in Asia, strong in flights.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Agoda is stronger in hotels in Southeast Asia; Trip.com is stronger in flights and China.

competitors.name: Airbnb
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Agoda offers both hotels and homes with deals; Airbnb has a stronger brand for homes.

pmLessons: Focus can beat size. Agoda wins in Asia by knowing local hotels, payments and languages better than global rivals.
Winning on price brings users, but trust keeps them. Support failures undo cheap prices.
Inside a group, sister brands can cover different regions instead of fighting each other.
Prepaid bookings give cash early but raise the stakes when a booking goes wrong.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you grow Agoda's share of Indian travellers going to Southeast Asia?
interviewQuestions.hint: Segment travellers, compare with MakeMyTrip, pick levers (UPI, bundles, trust, language), and measure conversion and repeat rate.

interviewQuestions.question: Agoda and Booking.com have the same owner. Should they merge?
interviewQuestions.hint: Think about brand, regions, supply sharing, tech costs and customer confusion. Pick a side with reasons.

interviewQuestions.question: Guests often complain that hotels cannot find their booking. How do you fix it?
interviewQuestions.hint: Map where the booking breaks (sync, wholesale supply), add confirmation checks, measure failure rate.

interviewQuestions.question: What north star would you pick for Agoda?
interviewQuestions.hint: Stayed room nights, not bookings or revenue, broken into traffic, conversion, repeat and stay success.

interviewQuestions.question: Should Agoda show non-refundable rooms first because they are cheaper?
interviewQuestions.hint: Weigh conversion against cancellation complaints and trust; propose an A/B test with guardrails.
